title: Fail-closed no-egress guard + local_only scope marking + egress_posture MCP tool + .well-known capability publication
priority_note: Highest-value story in the epic. #331 shipped agent autonomy over KB content while egress stayed uncontrolled AND undiscoverable - an agent can harvest a DNA file today with no supported way to check where it goes first. This story closes that, and it is the one capability that cannot be replaced by careful configuration. It therefore does NOT wait on US-41.2/US-41.3: the classifier, the fail-closed guard and egress_posture are implementable against TODAY's resolved (hardcoded vendor) endpoints, and posture reporting is strictly more truthful early. It is extended, not rewritten, as 41.2/41.3 make endpoints configurable.
background: Loopctl.Provider.Admission (lib/loopctl/provider/admission.ex, US-37.1 / GH #352) already sits immediately before every model-provider Req.post: anthropic.ex:118 guards :139, embedding_client.ex:91 and :101 guard :109 and :133. That makes it the correct chokepoint. CRITICALLY it is FAIL-OPEN BY DESIGN (admission.ex:81-97, fail_open/2 at :183) - it is a burst shedder whose job is to shed load without ever blocking legitimate traffic. An egress guard needs the OPPOSITE failure semantics. Fusing the two decisions would mean a Hammer or SystemConfig hiccup silently degrades the privacy guarantee to 'allow', turning a guarantee into a hope. The guard must therefore be a SEPARATE check at the same call sites that cannot inherit the fail-open path. Two grounded constraints shape the design: (a) Admission itself was added site-by-site and is consequently MISSED at webhooks/req_delivery.ex:43, verification/github_actions.ex:17 and secrets/fly_adapter.ex:60,112 - a guarantee enforced by per-call-site convention regresses the first time someone adds a Req call; (b) UrlGuard (net/url_guard.ex, GHSA-jh42-wf7g-f5rg) blocks loopback and every private range unconditionally, so the SSRF policy and the locality policy must be one module, not two that contradict each other.

story.as_a: an agent about to harvest a user's private documents
story.i_want_to: mark the target scope local_only, have loopctl HARD-REFUSE any provider call that would send that data to a non-local endpoint, and query the instance's egress posture before I start
story.so_that: private data cannot leave the boundary by misconfiguration or by a wrong base_url, and I can verify locality first instead of trusting it

rationale: A privacy tier that depends on the operator configuring three endpoints correctly is not a guarantee. Fail-closed enforcement plus a machine-readable posture surface converts it into one an agent can verify - which is the only form that works on a platform with no UI.

acceptance_criteria.description: A local_only marking exists at tenant and project scope, settable via a new MCP tool + matching JSON API endpoint (no UI). Default off everywhere; the hosted instance behaves exactly as today until a scope opts in. ROLES ARE ASYMMETRIC because the two transitions are not symmetric in trust: ENABLING local_only (tightening) is role :orchestrator or above, while DISABLING/CLEARING it is role :user - clearing the flag is exactly the self-widening move AC-41.4.5 forbids for the allowlist, and it would let an agent re-open egress one tool call before a harvest while US-41.7's witnessed claim faithfully attested the weakened posture. Both transitions are recorded in the audit log with actor and scope. Tests assert NO agent-role path clears local_only through any tool or endpoint.

Scope resolution is defined, not left per-call-site: the effective marking is the MOST RESTRICTIVE of the tenant and project markings (project local_only OR tenant local_only), a project can NEVER relax a tenant-level local_only, and any row or operation with no project (articles.project_id is nullable = tenant-wide, article.ex:19; memories have no required project association) inherits the TENANT marking. Because the guarded call sites carry no project context today (EmbeddingClient.generate_embedding/2 and Llm.Anthropic.call/N reach Admission with tenant_id only), the scope is THREADED through the embedding and chat APIs by this story, and endpoint resolution is scope-aware (project settings override tenant settings) so a local_only project inside an otherwise-vendor tenant has a configuration that can actually satisfy the guard rather than being permanently egress_blocked with no remediation. A test covers each combination: project-marked, tenant-marked, both, neither, and project-less.

When a scope is local_only, every outbound model-provider call whose resolved endpoint is not classified local is refused with {:error, :egress_blocked} BEFORE the Req.post. The check is FAIL-CLOSED: if the endpoint cannot be classified, or if the classification machinery itself errors, the call is REFUSED. A test forces the classifier to raise and asserts the call is blocked, not admitted.

The guard is a SEPARATE decision from Provider.Admission's fail-open rate check, and it is enforced at a SINGLE MANDATORY CHOKEPOINT rather than by per-call-site convention: all tenant-content egress routes through one wrapper (a Req request step or a Loopctl.Provider.post/3 wrapper) that performs the check, and a static test or Credo check asserts NO Req.post / Req.request / Req.get call exists anywhere in lib/ outside that wrapper's explicit allowlist. Admission's fail_open/2 path can never admit a call the egress guard would refuse. A test asserts that with the admission backend fully unavailable (fail-open triggered), a local_only scope with a non-local endpoint is still BLOCKED, and a second test adds a new raw Req call to a fixture module and asserts the static check FAILS - proving the check is load-bearing.

Locality classification separates the two concepts the epic must not conflate - NETWORK locality and TENANT OWNERSHIP: (a) network-local means loopback and private-range hosts plus the deployment LOCAL_ENDPOINT_ALLOWLIST; (b) tenant-declared trusted endpoints are a PER-TENANT list of hosts the tenant attests are their own (their VPS, tailscale funnel, or domain), settable at role :user only. This second list is mandatory, not optional: on the HOSTED instance the server's loopback and private ranges are the OPERATOR's network, so a hosted tenant's own Ollama/TEI box is reachable ONLY via a public hostname, and a network-locality-only definition would hard-block every real hosted local_only tenant - contradicting the epic's central claim that Axis A ships on the hosted service unchanged. api.openai.com and api.anthropic.com are never local and may never be declared. The posture report and the US-41.7 custody claim LABEL the two distinctly ('network-local' vs 'tenant-declared, not network-local') and must never present a declared endpoint as network-local. The deployment allowlist remains DEPLOYMENT-scoped and READ-ONLY to every role including :user - it is the trust root, and an agent must never widen its own allowlist; a test asserts no API path mutates it.

egress_blocked degrades safely and legibly WITHOUT poisoning the circuit breaker: Knowledge.breaker_countable?/1 gains an explicit clause returning FALSE for :egress_blocked (knowledge.ex:7941's catch-all returns true today, so a brand-new atom would record a provider failure toward the per-tenant breaker and emit the fleet-wide [:loopctl, :llm, :provider_error] storm signal - exactly the failure :rate_limited_local was exempted for at :7939). A permanent local configuration refusal must never open the breaker. The interactive path falls back like the existing circuit-open case (keyword search, never a 500); harvesting fails the ITEM with an agent-readable reason naming the scope and the offending endpoint. A test asserts a blocked call records no provider-error telemetry and never opens the breaker. No data is sent in any path.

The degraded response is explicitly labelled and never a bare empty list. Whenever the semantic path is unavailable (egress_blocked, circuit open, or embedding fallback), the response meta names the reason AND the offending endpoint, and - critically for the tenant this epic targets - flags that keyword fallback does NOT cover encrypted-tier rows (US-41.6 AC-41.6.2 removes encrypted bodies from the FTS index, so a local_only + encrypt_body tenant would otherwise receive a successful-looking 200 with a structurally impossible-to-populate result set that reads as 'nothing in your KB'). A cross-story test with local_only + encrypt_body asserts the response states that encrypted-tier content was excluded rather than returning a silent empty/partial result.

An egress_posture MCP tool + matching JSON endpoint reports: the resolved embedding and chat endpoints for the calling tenant, whether each is network-local or tenant-declared, the deployment allowlist, the tenant's declared trusted endpoints, and per-scope local_only status. Endpoints are shown; keys never are. This is how an agent verifies locality BEFORE harvesting. It is a READ tool available at agent role.

There is exactly ONE egress policy module and every outbound path consults it: the provider guard, the US-41.2 probe, ingestion, and (in US-41.5) webhook delivery. It composes the SSRF denylist with the locality decision, so the deployment allowlist and the tenant's declared trusted endpoints - and ONLY those - can carve specific hosts/CIDRs out of UrlGuard's loopback/private/CGNAT/link-local/Fly-6PN denylist (GHSA-jh42-wf7g-f5rg stays closed for everything else). A second, divergent URL policy anywhere in lib/ is a review failure. A test asserts an undeclared tenant still cannot reach a private-range host and a declared one can.

The .well-known/loopctl discovery endpoint (US-26.0.4) publishes instance CAPABILITIES: the FIXED set of supported embedding dimensions (US-41.1 AC-41.1.3), whether tenant-supplied endpoints are permitted, and which tiers exist - so an agent can discover the instance's constraints BEFORE authenticating. No tenant-specific data appears there.

Every new table or column introduced by this story (local_only markings, declared trusted endpoints, egress-decision records) carries tenant_id, uses the enable_rls/1 macro (ENABLE, not FORCE, per CLAUDE.md's Multi-Tenant Rules), and has a tenant-isolation test asserting tenant A cannot read or mutate tenant B's marking. Deployment-scoped state (the allowlist) is explicitly NOT tenant data and lives outside RLS by design.

Hot-path cost is one cheap classification per provider call with NO network or DB round-trip, and the resolution policy is stated rather than left open: the endpoint host is resolved and classified ONCE at config time (the US-41.2 probe), the resulting pinned IP set is CACHED with a TTL alongside the resolved settings, and the call-time check reads that cache and connects with UrlGuard.pinned_request_opts/1 so the IP actually connected to is the IP that was classified (closing resolve-then-connect / DNS-rebinding TOCTOU). A stale or missing cache entry is a fail-closed refusal, never a hot-path DNS lookup. A benchmark or timing assertion documents the cached path.

technical_notes: The guard lives at ONE wrapper (AC-41.4.4), not replicated at anthropic.ex:118 / embedding_client.ex:91,101 by convention. Those sites call the wrapper; the static check keeps future call sites from bypassing it. Admission stays a separate with-clause so the two failure modes never share a code path.

Classification resolves the endpoint HOST and pins the resulting IPs at config time (AC-41.4.12), so DNS pointing a public name at a private address (or rebinding between resolve and connect) cannot fool it. Reuse UrlGuard.pinned_request_opts/1 rather than inventing a second mechanism.

This story covers MODEL-PROVIDER egress only. Webhook delivery bypasses Admission entirely (webhooks/req_delivery.ex:43) and is handled in US-41.5 - the docs and the posture report must NOT claim total egress control until 41.5 lands.

egress_posture is a read tool and should be available at agent role: an agent must be able to check locality with the key it already has, or the whole verify-before-harvest workflow fails. WRITING local_only is a different matter - see AC-41.4.1's asymmetric roles.
Record every egress_blocked decision in the audit log - US-41.7 turns these records into the custody claim.

Dependency note: this story deliberately does NOT depend on US-41.2/US-41.3. Implement the classifier, guard, policy module and posture surface against today's resolved endpoints; extend the resolution inputs when configurable endpoints land.
